newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end quiet, edgy trading mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end quiet, edgy trading mixed.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended quiet but edgy pit trading mixed, with most units showing little change.
Traders pinned the limited movement to trepidation about Wednesday's September U.S. consumer price index, which is expected to rise 0.3 percent overall and in the core rate.
The market late glossed over the 0.9-percent rise in weekly retail sales, as reported in Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc's Redbook index.
December Treasury bond futures briefly ticked down to the day's low at 110-12/32 after midday but lacked followthrough.
Some traders tied the erosion, which occurred on dealer sales that featured one firm selling roughly 2,000 contracts, partly to hedging.

Others called it a technical trade as nearby T-bonds peeked below minor support near 110-14/32. Still others noted positioning before the inflation figures and after U.S. stocks had faded from an early upward extension.

"The technicals have been friendly," said one floor broker in T-bond futures. "The fundamentals haven't been that great. I personally think it topped out a couple days ago, but it's the technicals that are holding it up."
He also said he thought the long end might have more potential on the downside on a strong CPI figure "because there doesn't appear to be too many shorts left in here."
Futures showed muted reaction during the morning to the rise in the September Atlanta Federal Reserve business activity index to 5.8 from a revised 4.9 in August.
Nor did the market move much when weekly BTM/Schroders chain store sales rose 0.3 percent, brokers said.
The rise early on Tuesday in crude oil prices to post-Gulf War highs may have made some longs temporarily nervous, but the fuel subsequently gave back the gains.

At the end of pit trading, DecembertT-bonds lost 3/32 to 110-16/32, T-notes ended flat at 108-07/32, muni-bonds fell 8/32 to 114-14/32, March T-bills ended down two basis points at 94.78, and Eurodollars gave up one basis point to 94.27. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
